QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_22

question.text: Year 1 of a Cat III AIF produces return of 20%, Year 2 is -5%, Year 3 is +11%. The HWM concept would require incentive fees be paid on Year 3 ONLY IF:

answer.text: Year 3 NAV exceeds Year 1 NAV (the prior HWM)

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook introduces HWM so that incentive fees are not charged after a loss until NAV recovers past the relevant previous high. Example 3 applies HWM as an additional threshold alongside the reference hurdle, with incentive fees computed only on the positive excess over the minimum eligible NAV, taken as the higher of HWM and the reference hurdle. After Year 1's 20% gain and a Year 2 drawdown of -5%, full Year 3 incentive eligibility requires NAV to exceed the Year 1 NAV that became the prior HWM. The Trap: Exceeding only the beginning NAV, having a positive Year 3 NAV, or recording any Year 3 gain does not satisfy the HWM threshold once the prior high has been set. Note: Per workbook pages 173 and 175 covering HWM and Example 3.
